  artifact is uploaded. 0.114.2 published on the old name roughly an hour before this landed, so
  **0.114.3 is the first tag to run through `publish.yaml`.** The fix is a one-field human edit
  (PyPI → gen-worker → Manage → Publishing → Workflow name); a 403 costs nothing but a re-run of
  publish on the same tag.

*Attributed after the cut (pgw#1226): this fragment was in the tagged tree and was not assembled into the section at cut time.*

- Vocabulary sweep (pgw#1244, DESIGN-RULINGS §1.39). Docs, comments and docstrings only —
  no identifier, wire or behaviour change. "Tree" no longer names a checkpoint's contents
  (a manifest is a flat file list): `writer.py` says "one dtype per checkpoint",
  `lint_cell_key_layout_fence.py` says "snapshot tree" like the rest of the tree, and the
  `layouts` map's `"*"` is documented as "every component" rather than "the whole tree" —
  it is one level deep, keyed by component. Two stale `flavor` survivals that contradicted
  live code are corrected: `SourceRepo`'s docstring no longer advertises a `#flavor`
  selector that `refuse_flavor_selector` rejects (or the deleted tensorhub
  `docs/checkpoint-flavors.md`), and `docs/host-integration.md` no longer lists a `flavor`
  key that `cli/listing.py`'s tuple does not contain.

## 0.114.2 (2026-08-13) — **the compiled-graph format ships as v1 under a qualified name** — DESIGN-RULINGS §1.38b, the last identity contract to settle before the family train mints

> **CUT FROM A PINNED COMMIT: `a98f232f`.** 28 commits since `v0.114.1`, assembled from 5 fragments.
> Cut under the standing enqueue freeze (pgw#1226).
>
> **Re-pinned twice, on purpose.** The first assembly consumed 2 fragments; pgw#1236 and pgw#1229
> merged underneath the cut while it sat in the merge queue, then pgw#1227 (the comment cull) landed
> too. Shipping any of those passes would have put their code in this wheel with no entry in this
> section and re-dated their fragments to the NEXT release — a silent release note in both
> directions, which is exactly what happened to 0.114.0 and what `docs/releasing.md` exists to
> prevent. Re-pinned and re-assembled each time instead. That is pgw#1226's mechanism, twice over:
> a cut cannot hold still while lanes merge underneath it.
>
> **CORRECTION TO THE 0.114.1 SECTION BELOW.** It states that 0.114.0 capped a `#fragment` at 64
> and so could not parse its own 66-character `cg-key-v1` key. **That is wrong.** 0.114.0 shipped
> `MAX_FRAGMENT_LEN = 127` — PR #764's widening rode into the tag at `a0c7b86d` — so keys parsed
> fine on that wheel. 0.114.0's real defects were the pgw#1230 `format` divergence (fatal: a
> completed mint armed nothing) and a scheme-PINNED `is_key` that disagreed with tensorhub's shared
> corpus on 8 of its 26 vectors. The published conclusion is unchanged and still stands:
> **0.114.0 must not be used for a mint.**
>
> **The free window was verified, not assumed**, before the format re-key: `cell_store` held 0 rows,
> `cell_receipts` held 9 rows all of the retired `ck1-` scheme, no `cg-key-v1` object existed
> anywhere durable, and no tensorhub code reads or compares the axis. That window closes the moment
> the family train mints, which is why this is the last identity contract to settle before it.

- Typing: **`WireRef` reaches the surfaces it was minted for.** The NewType has
  existed since gw#492 carrying the docstring *"Annotate wire/residency key
  surfaces with WireRef so mixing raw and normalized strings fails mypy"* — and
  had **zero annotation sites in production**. It is now the type of the ref on
  `ModelStore`'s whole public surface (30 params), of the hub-resolved
  `snapshots` maps, and of what `wire_ref`/`binding_wire_refs`/
  `component_overrides` state they MINT. Annotations and casts only; no logic
  changed.
- The producers were the root cause and are fixed first: `wire_ref` returned
  plain `str` while two of its three branches already returned normal form, so
  every consumer downstream started from an erased type. The civitai/modelscope
  branch ASSERTS normal form rather than deriving it, and now says so in one
  visible `WireRef(...)` instead of widening the function's whole return type.
- `residency.py` is deliberately still keyed by plain `str` and is its own
  unit; the raw→normal hops are a handful of stated casts at that boundary
  rather than a claim spread through the store.
- This lands **behind** pgw#1217 on purpose. The conversion made that defect's
  two client-ref sites a compile error without being aimed at them, and
  suppressing them would have been an annotation asserting something the code
  did not yet do. The behavior fix landed first; the types now hold it true.

- **pgw#1227: the comment purge — tracker-issue citations leave the code.** Paul,
  2026-08-13: *"deleting a lot of the comments ... delete the comments that are
  more incidental / historical. That's just adding historical noise to our
  codebase honestly."* A mechanical pass strips `pgw#NNN` / `th#NNN` / `ie#NNN`
  citation tokens out of comment and docstring prose across 431 files, keeping
  every fact they were attached to. Every edit is proven comment-only by an
  AST-equivalence gate: both sides are parsed, all docstrings stripped, and
  `ast.dump()` compared, so executable semantics are identical by construction.

- **pgw#1227 / th#1376's worker half (HARD CUT): the topology wire speaks ONE
  spelling.** `gen_worker.topology` no longer accepts the pre-rename
  `group_degree` / `groups` keys: `LEGACY_KEY_GPUS_PER_GROUP`,
  `LEGACY_KEY_EXECUTION_GROUPS`, the `_aliased` dual reader, its
  `topology_alias_disagree` refusal and its per-decode deprecation warning are
  deleted, and both names now fall through the CLOSED key set to
  `topology_unknown_field` — refused BY NAME rather than read as absent, which
  is the silent one-slot downgrade the closed set exists to prevent. The hub
  half shipped with th#1376 (`topology.Parse`'s key set is already the four
  canonical names), so this removes a divergence rather than creating one: the
  vendored conformance corpus moves its eight `divergent` vectors into `agreed`
  as `topology_unknown_field` refusals on both sides, and the defect ledger is
  empty. **The corpus is vendored byte-identically in tensorhub
  (`internal/orchestrator/topology/testdata/`) and must land there in the same
  window.**

- **pgw#1227 (HARD CUT, BEHAVIOUR CHANGE): there is no pickle reader left in the
  package.** Paul, 2026-08-12: *"keep pickles banned"* — refuse always; the
  sanctioned remedy for a legacy repo is to MIRROR it without the pickle.
  `convert/classifier.py` already refused a pickle-only repo with `pickle_only`,
  but two component-level doors bypassed that gate and converted the pickle
  instead: `repackage._load_component_state_dict`'s `<bin_base>.bin` fallback and
  `writer.iter_component_tensors`' `_PICKLE_EXTS` branch. Both now raise the same
  typed `pickle_only:<file>` refusal, naming the mirror-without-the-pickle
  remedy, and `materialize_pickle_to_safetensors` / `PICKLE_CACHE_DIR` are
  deleted outright. **A benign `.bin` is refused exactly like a poisoned one** —
  the safe/unsafe distinction can only be drawn by READING the file, which is the
  act being banned. The tree-scan guard now asserts ZERO `torch.load` sites
  rather than one `weights_only=True` site. **Consumer impact:** the conversion
  endpoint declares `bin_base` for seven families in
  `training-endpoints/conversion/src/conversion/declarations/families.py`; those
  declarations are now inert and their sources must be mirrored as safetensors.

- **pgw#1229: the hub's typed refusal now reaches the human instead of dying one stack frame away.** Two production `dj-pipeline/make-video` invokes died `fatal` with a total diagnosis of `HTTPError: 403 Client Error: Forbidden for url: .../api/v1/media/urls`, while the body the hub had actually sent named both the code and the remedy — *"worker capabilities must use the exact input-asset resolver"*. `resp.raise_for_status()` threw both away. New `gen_worker.hub_error` owns the envelope parse ONCE (`{"error":{"code","message","request_id"}}` and pgw#987's bare-string publish/gin shape), exports `raise_for_hub_error(resp, what=...)` as the replacement for `raise_for_status()` on calls to our hub, and raises `HubApiError` whose one-line `str()` leads with the code. `executor._map_exception` gained its arm, so that string is what lands in `request_state.error_message_safe`; retry class follows `http_origin` (a non-envelope answer came from a proxy in front of the hub, so it is retryable — a hub-authored 403 is not). The three duplicate envelope parsers (`callout`, `presigned_upload`, `hubio.client`) now delegate, and the dataset/blob auth refusals carry the hub's sentence instead of just its number. Sweep result recorded: every remaining `raise_for_status()` in gen_worker and the shipped endpoints is a presigned-object download, civitai, or a local llama-server — no hub envelope to lose — except dj-pipeline's `_Run._wire`, which pgw#1220 deletes.

- **pgw#1232 (DESIGN-RULINGS §1.38b): the compiled-graph artifact format starts at v1, and its
  axis name is qualified.** `aot_serve.ARTIFACT_FORMAT = 3` becomes
  `COMPILED_GRAPH_FORMAT = 1`, and the metadata key and arm axis it is stamped/compared under
  rename from the generic `format` to **`compiled_graph_format`** (both read from one symbol,
  `COMPILED_GRAPH_FORMAT_KEY`, so the stamp and the comparison cannot drift into two spellings).
  Paul: *"we are pre-launch, so we should be on v1 for everything, including our compiled-graph
  format."* The version records the first contract we ship, not the count of abandoned internal
  prototypes. **Hard cut:** no 3→1 mapping, no accepted set — an artifact of a retired format is
  refused by name, which is what makes a v1 reader unable to consume one. The ruling names the
  generic `format` as what let pgw#1230 compare the AOT package schema against an unrelated
  torch-inductor semantic-cache epoch, costing a fully compiled 4-class mint. Verified free before
  shipping: `cell_store` 0 rows, zero `cg-key-v1` objects anywhere durable, and no hub code reads
  or compares the axis.
- **pgw#1232: the two 64-bit chokepoints under the `graph` key axis are derived and documented
  rather than inherited.** `graph_hash._DIGEST_HEX` and `aot_serve.class_hash`'s own truncation are
  both 16 hex, and the axis has the MINIMUM of the two — so widening either alone re-keys the whole
  corpus and buys nothing. Kept at 64 bits with the birthday bound written at both sites
  (P ≈ N²/2⁶⁵: ~3e-12 at 10⁴ graph classes, ~3e-8 at 10⁶), and with the both-or-neither rule stated
  where a future widener will read it.

- **pgw#1236: formula parity is pinned.** CI now pins the shared
  Tensorhub/python-gen-worker conformance corpus to one digest, so a one-sided
  ledger edit fails before either language can quietly certify a different
  contract.

## 0.114.1 (2026-08-13) — **the `format` arm axis had TWO derivations, so every freshly minted cell compiled fine and then armed NOTHING** — plus the ref fragment is finally wide enough to carry the key it exists to carry, and the compiled-graph key grammar becomes a fenced cross-repo contract with tensorhub

> **CUT FROM A PINNED COMMIT: `c064a436`.** 24 commits since `v0.114.0`. Cut under an ENQUEUE
> FREEZE (pgw#1226): the 0.114.0 cut was ejected from the merge queue FOUR times as `UNMERGEABLE`,
> because a cut DELETES every `changelog.d/` fragment while every lane PR MODIFIES one, so the cut
> conflicts with all of them by construction. Freezing enqueues for the duration costs less than one
> ejection.
>
> **READ THIS IF YOU ARE CUTTING NEXT — `v0.114.0` is not where its own release notes say it is.**
> The 0.114.0 section below states it was cut from the pinned commit `73f826e1`, but the TAG was
> pushed at **`a0c7b86d`** (PR #764, the `cg-key-v1` scheme rename), 8 commits later. The published
> 0.114.0 wheel therefore contains code its section never describes — exactly the silent release note
> `docs/releasing.md` forbids, arriving through the "re-point the tag at master's tip" door rather
> than the changelog one. Nothing is being rewritten retroactively; it is recorded here so the next
> `git rev-list v0.114.0..HEAD` is read with the right expectation. The practical consequence: the
> **scheme half** of pgw#1213 already shipped in 0.114.0, and the fragment says so.
>
> **What 0.114.0 shipped broken, and this fixes.** The 0.114.0 wheel is pod-verified and carries
> `cg-key-v1` — a 66-character key — while its own ref grammar capped a `#fragment` at 64, so
> `parse_cell_ref` returned `("", "")` and a pod could not name the family of an artifact it had
> just armed. It also carries the `format` divergence, so a completed mint arms nothing. Both are
> fixed here. **0.114.0 should not be used for a mint.**

- Typing: the two HARNESS doubles that were **wholly unchecked** are checked.
  `tests.harness.cell_hub` and `tests.harness.adopt_rig` sat in the
  `ignore_errors` burn-down, so nothing in them could fail — a bogus attribute
  plus a `reveal_type` injected into `cell_hub.py` still produced `Success: no
  issues found`. `cell_hub.py` additionally carried 30
  `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comments that suppressed nothing (the module
  exemption already did, and `warn_unused_ignores` is off for tests), so they
  read as diligence while being decoration. Ratchet 314 → 312.
- `cell_hub`'s state is a declared `CellHubServer(ThreadingHTTPServer)` instead
  of seven attributes bolted onto a stock server after construction. A typo in
  any of the handler's thirty reads used to be an `AttributeError` raised inside
  a request thread — the double failing in a way that looks like the system
  under test failing. Now `srv.objcts` is `error: "CellHubServer" has no
  attribute "objcts"; maybe "objects"?`. `record_checkpoint` moves onto the
  server beside the state it mutates, and the duplicate `slock(srv)` spelling of
  `with srv.lock` dies.
- `adopt_rig` patched two module objects twice: `executor.activity_mod` IS
  `gen_worker.activity` and `executor.provision` IS `gen_worker.models.provision`
  (verified `is`-identical — the executor resolves both attributes at call
  time), so each pair was one patch written twice, reaching through an implicit
  re-export to do it. One patch each now.

- **pgw#1206 C2: the record queries leave the job engine, and a third copy of
  the VRAM probe dies.** `Executor._record_refs` / `_records_holding` /
  `_record_in_use` become free functions in `gen_worker.models.records`, taking
  exactly what they read (records, jobs, residency) instead of a back-reference.
  `Executor._vram_allocated` is **deleted outright**: it duplicated
  `gen_worker.models.memory.cuda_allocated_bytes`, which is the canonical export
  and already the probe `cli/serve.py` uses; its five call sites now use it too.
  `shutdown_instances` and `_vacate_record` deliberately stay on the executor —
  both call `abandon_background_mint`, which is inside th#1834's frozen
  Phase-3 region, and dragging a frozen method across a module seam is what the
  fence forbids.

- **pgw#1213: the key scheme is `cg-key-v1`.** The per-entry key scheme minted by
  `cell_key` is renamed `ek1` -> `cg-key-v1`, landed before the `v0.114.0` tag
  existed and before anything published, so no artifact was ever addressed by
  `ek1`. The `v0.114.0` tag landed on this commit, so this half is already in the 0.114.0
  wheel; the grammar work in the next bullet is what is new here. `is_key` generalizes with it: the
  scheme token now contains hyphens, so the grammar is `<scheme>-<56 lowercase
  hex>` matched from the RIGHT (the fixed-width digest is anchored to the end and
  everything before it is the scheme) and no reader may split a key on `-` or
  slice a fixed prefix width off one.
- **pgw#1213 / th#1897: the compiled-graph key grammar is a cross-repo contract, and
  the ref fragment is wide enough to carry a key.** `MAX_FRAGMENT_LEN` moves 64 -> 96
  in the new leaf module `gen_worker.refgrammar`, mirroring tensorhub's
  `internal/refgrammar.MaxFragmentLen`: a key IS the `#fragment` of
  `root/family-<f>#<key>`, and `cg-key-v1-` + 56 hex is 66 bytes, so under the old cap
  `parse_cell_ref` raised and returned `("", "")` — a pod could not name the family of
  the artifact it had just armed, with no hub involved. `is_key` is scheme-AGNOSTIC
  (th#1183): it refuses SHAPE, never scheme, so a newer fleet's key stays addressable
  by an older hub and the two can ship in different windows. Both grammars are pinned
  by `tests/testdata/compiled_graph_key_vectors.json` (26 vectors, vendored
  byte-identically in tensorhub, digest-fenced by `scripts/check_grammar_corpus_digest.py`
  in `fast gates` and by `scripts/grammar-vector-drift.sh` from the hub side). The arm
  token's disjointness from the key space now rides its DIGEST WIDTH (64 hex, not 56)
  rather than its `arm2-` prefix, which a scheme-agnostic grammar cannot honour.

- **pgw#1215 (th#1834 Phase 3): the mint's shared substrate leaves the modules that are about to
  die.** Phase 3 replaces the out-of-process mint driver with a serving parent that supervises
  compile children directly, one graph class each — at which point `mint_child`, `mint_process` and
  `mint_delegate` fall out. Measured first: **they are ~20 % substrate, not driver.** `mint_process`
  is also the tree's home for the parent↔child *vocabulary* and `mint_child` for the child-side
  *preflight*, and five modules that SURVIVE the rewrite already import both — `executor`,
  `boot_key`, `boot_adopt`, `measure_child`, `local_serve` — plus `boot_trace_child` and both
  operator rigs.

  So the substrate moves out first, on its own, with no behaviour change: `child_contract.py`
  (`MintSlot`, `CompileSpec`, `slot_subjects`, `MintFrame`, `frame_line`) and `child_preflight.py`
  (`PreflightRefused`, `select_specs`, `bind_slots`, `assert_slots_resolvable`,
  `pick_compile_target`). With it gone the driver's removal is a **cut**; with it still inside, that
  removal would have been an untangle — a deletion obliged to preserve two thirds of what it deletes,
  which is how a rewrite acquires a compatibility shim nobody asked for.

  **A defect fixed on the way out.** `boot_trace_child` and `measure_child` reached into `mint_child`
  for the same five preflight symbols through **function-local imports at three call sites**, because
  importing `mint_child` at module scope drags the whole compile brain in behind it — the shape §1.17
  forbids, and unfixable while the checks lived beside the driver. They are ordinary top-of-file
  imports now, and the module that owns the mint has stopped being a library for children that do not
  mint.

  **Renames** (no aliases, pre-launch): `CompileCellSpec` → `CompileSpec` and `MintChildRefused` →
  `PreflightRefused`. The refusal is deliberately NOT called `MintRefused` — that name is live in
  `aot_contract` for "every declared graph class refused", and one name for both would make "this
  subject cannot be built here" and "nothing compiled" indistinguishable at the exit-code boundary
  with no test going red.

- **pgw#1215 step 2a: the mint's packaging tail becomes callable — `aot_mint.pack_graph_classes`.**
  Phase 3's compile child traces and compiles its own share in ONE address space (that is the whole
  point: the `torch.export.save`/`load` pair is deleted rather than relocated), so the child ends up
  holding the `_MintedEntry` rows and has to turn them into artifacts itself. Left inline in
  `_mint_cell`, the child would have had to re-implement packaging — and two packagers is exactly
  the divergence per-graph-class identity exists to rule out.

  **A move, not a design.** The 136-line tail is lifted verbatim; a line-by-line diff against
  `origin/master` shows exactly one changed line (`progress.pool_ledger` becomes the `pool_ledger`
  parameter). The seam is not invented either: `_export_entry` already RETURNS a `_MintedEntry` and
  `trace_for_key` already builds them internally, so the two halves have always spoken this type.
  Ordering, refusals, `timings` keys and the phase event are unchanged.

- **Fixed: a client-supplied ref is a residency key, and it was not normalized
  where it enters.** `payload.source` / `text_encoder` / `candidate` and every
  `lora overlay.ref` arrive as free-form strings from the job payload. The
  executor took them verbatim and used each for two things that both require
  normal form: the `snapshots` lookup (that map is keyed by normalized refs —
  it is built from `wire_ref`/`binding_wire_refs`) and the residency key passed
  to `store.ensure_local`. A non-normal spelling of the same model therefore
  MISSED its snapshot and minted a **second residency identity** for the same
  weights — a redundant multi-GB download, a second disk-GC entry, and two
  cache identities where the hub believes there is one. That is the th#736
  mechanic `api.binding.rebind_pick`'s own docstring warns about. `acme/repo:prod`
  is the cheapest witness: `prod` is the grammar default, so it is elided and
  both spellings are one model by definition.
- Both inlets now call `normalize_model_ref` at the boundary, and a ref the
  grammar cannot parse is a named `ValidationError` naming its field rather
  than a bogus residency key nothing can resolve. gw#491 had already fixed this
  invariant one level down — for the DIGEST spelling, three lines from the
  adapter site ("one adapter must never mint two cache identities"); it left
  the REF spelling open, and this closes it.
- Found by reading during the pgw#1202 typing work, then found AGAIN
  independently by the type checker: annotating `ModelStore`'s ref surface as
  `WireRef` makes exactly these two call sites a compile error without being
  aimed at them. Those two errors disappearing is this fix's acceptance test.

- **th#1871 P1's worker half — the serve POSTURE is typed and rides
  `JobMetrics` (pgw#1225).** DESIGN-RULINGS §1.36 stage 2: *"a benchmark
  measured through a silent degradation is not a benchmark."* The deciding
  specimen is ie#707 — a family served on `sdpa` because flash-attn was absent
  from its image while its lane declared flash, and every number taken from those
  runs was filed as a measurement OF the flash lane. tensorhub now keys
  `endpoint_measurements` on a posture digest (th#1871 P2, `4f57e6e6`), and until
  this change every `source='serve'` row got the UNREPORTED posture: the hub's
  reducer deliberately refuses to parse the prose the worker already emits into
  `worker_activity_events.detail`, because parsing prose to recover structure is
  the defect that table exists to end. So this is a change of REPRESENTATION,
  not of instrumentation — every field was already known, and already said, in
  words, on a channel no decision reads.

  New wire message `MeasuredPosture` on `JobMetrics.posture` (field 24),
  mirroring Go's `measurement.Posture` field-for-field so the digest needs no
  translation layer. It carries the resolved lane, the attention backend
  ENGAGED and the one WANTED, the compile state applied and declared, the
  residency rung, the ORDERED list of levers reached for, per-component
  applied-vs-bound quant, and a typed VRAM shortfall (`needed N, had M`). Not
  named `ServePosture`: that message already exists and is the hub→worker
  operator eager-only command (§4.32).

- **New public reporter: `gen_worker.report_attention_backend(component,
  backend, *, wanted=...)`.** `report_applied_attention` reports SPARSITY
  (`dense` / `sparse-k<N>`) and raises on `"sdpa"` — correctly, because a kernel
  is not a sparsity budget, and 23 of 29 families consequently reported nothing
  at all. The kernel is a second axis and gets a second reporter. Ecosystem
  spellings (`flash_attention_2`, `FlashAttention-3`, `torch_sdpa`, `math`) are
  normalized rather than refused; a token tensorhub does not share still raises,
  because that is a fourth vocabulary and the reporter is the last place to stop
  one. `AppliedAttention.mode` is now optional — a backend-only report says
  nothing about sparsity and must not read as a claim of dense.

- **The declared compile axis comes off BOTH hub statements.** `compile_state_wanted`
  reads the instructed lane's `+compiled` suffix, and falls back to the
  `required_compile` fence — because `RunJob.lane` is empty whenever the lane
  rides `HelloAck`'s `ModelResolution` instead of a per-request override
  (`scheduler_dispatch.go:1037`: `"" = policy`), and on that path the fence is
  the only thing that states the axis. Unstated stays EMPTY rather than
  defaulting to eager: a mismatch needs a stated expectation to violate, and
  inventing one would report every policy-dispatched request as a clean
  compiled-vs-eager agreement.

- **The PROACTIVE descent is reported.** `memory.place_pipeline` keeps the fit
  numbers its own decision was made on, and the executor records the posture for
  EVERY placement rather than only the OOM-demoted one. A pipeline that
  `select_auto_mode` put on the offload ladder never OOMs, so it reported
  nothing, served 2.5-4x slow, and its numbers were filed as a resident run —
  the largest silent degradation th#1871's census found.

- **The collapsed rungs get names.** `model_offload`, `group_offload` and
  `sequential` stop sharing the wire token `offload` (their prices differ by
  60%), and `vae_slicing` and `attention_fallback` get a wire representation at
  all. A degraded run now also logs one derived summary line — §1.36's amendment
  asks the worker to complain loudly, and the line is derived from the typed
  record so the two cannot disagree.

- **Cross-repo fence:** `tests/testdata/posture_wire_vectors.json` +
  `scripts/posture-vector-drift.sh`, vendored byte-identically in tensorhub. The
  DIGEST has exactly one implementation and it is the hub's — the worker pins
  the digests as opaque data and never derives them, because a second
  canonicalization of one object is two implementations free to disagree while
  both suites stay green (pgw#1188's topology divergence, one contract over).
  The ledger's `identity_rules` state which pairs of postures are one
  measurement; those are §1.36 decisions, not implementation details.

- Testing: `test_armed_target_install_pgw1093`'s three tests no longer change
  verdict with the box. They failed on any host exporting
  `GEN_WORKER_FORBID_CPU_OFFLOAD` and passed everywhere else — measured A/B on
  a dev box: **3 failed exported, 3 passed unset**. The chain was environmental
  end to end: an unreadable free-VRAM probe makes `place_pipeline` select
  `group_offload` (pgw#940 — an unmeasured card does not license residency),
  `group_offload` is unavailable so it falls back to `sequential`, and the real
  applier then raises `CpuOffloadForbidden`. None of that is what these tests
  assert, which is compile-target installation and eager posture.
- The fix is the seam `test_rung_ladder_pgw1206` already uses for this exact
  guard (the th#1043 pattern): the `boot` fixture stubs
  `apply_low_vram_config`, so the diffusers placement hooks — not the code
  under test — never run. Pinning free VRAM high instead does NOT work: it
  selects the resident rung and routes into `pipeline.to("cuda")`, which a
  cardless box cannot satisfy.
- The guard itself is deliberately unchanged. It is a ratified weights-locality
  tripwire (pgw#929), not configuration, and deleting it to quiet three tests
  would be fixing the wrong end. A test whose verdict depends on a box-wide env
  is measuring the box, not the code — the discipline pgw#1049 imposed for
  `PYTHONHASHSEED`, applied here.

- **pgw#1230 (P0): the `format` arm axis had TWO derivations, so every freshly minted
  cell failed to arm.** Two different facts shared the name `ARTIFACT_FORMAT`:
  `aot_serve.ARTIFACT_FORMAT` (the AOT cell metadata schema, which the child stamps) and
  `compile_cache.ARTIFACT_FORMAT` (the torch-inductor-cache producer format from gw#391,
  an ingredient of the JIT semantic cache tag). `fleet_cells.arm_identity` computed its
  `format` fact from the second and compared it against the first. Both were 2, so it
  passed by coincidence until pgw#1176 moved the cell schema to 3 — after which every
  freshly minted cell was refused at arm with `key_axis_divergence: format: child cell
  states '3', this runtime computed '2'`, served eager, and published nothing (observed
  on Cell Zero across all 4 z-image graph classes: compiled, quarantined, zero published).
  The arm axis now reads the producer's own symbol, and the inductor constant is renamed
  `compile_cache.SEMANTIC_TAG_FORMAT` — same value, so no cache tag churns — so the two
  facts can no longer be confused for one. **No key is orphaned:** `format` is an arm
  fact, never a cell-key axis (the axes are graph x sm x toolchain), so the four stamped
  `cg-key-v1` keys were always correct and a re-mint reproduces them byte-for-byte.

- **BREAKING (th#1842, vendored) — `SchedulerMessage.run_attempt` and the whole
  abandoned staged-dispatch surface are gone from the wire contract.** Tag 7 is
  `reserved` and so is the name, because a within-major retirement that leaves
  the number free lets the next field added there silently inherit a live wire
  tag. 24 orphaned declarations go with it (21 messages + the `WeightLane`,
  `ArmShape` and `SteadyBackend` enums, which were field types only inside
  deleted messages) — including `ExecutionSpec`, `EndpointRelease` and
  `ArtifactIdentity`. Nothing ever produced or consumed any of it: pgw's
  consumer half died in pgw#1206 D-1 and tensorhub deleted the producer in
  `ec978c68`. The generic exhaustiveness refusal in `lifecycle.on_message`
  stays, as ruled — it is not a per-message vestige, it covers every oneof this
  worker does not handle, and dropping such a message would discard tenant work
  against an accepted-or-result contract.

- **th#1867 S1 follow-up, caught by the merge queue itself: a green assertion about a deleted rung.**
  pgw#1206 D removed the bnb-nf4 rung while PR #757 sat in the queue. The queue re-ran against
  master's real tip and stayed green — but one parametrized case in
  `tests/test_descent_floor_th1867.py` still named `"nf4"` and **passed for a different reason than
  it was written for**: an unknown token also descends to `model_offload`. The upper-rung list is
  now DERIVED from `rung.LADDER`, so a rung added or deleted is covered automatically. A green
  assertion about a symbol that no longer exists is exactly the class this file was written to
  guard, and it took one merge to produce one.

- **th#1887: the behaviour-gate scanner can see the shape three gates were hiding in.**
  `BEHAVIOUR_GATES` is enforced bidirectionally, so an undeclared gate fails CI — but the
  scanner was purely syntactic: a read counted only inside an `if`/`while`/ternary/`assert`
  test, a comprehension guard, or the return of a bool-annotated or predicate-named
  function. Three real gates lived in a shape it could not see at all — read into a local,
  then discriminated against a set of known strings — and all three sat misfiled as
  STANDALONE while living in serving hot-path modules. A registry that cannot see a whole
  gate SHAPE is worse than one that misses three gates: it reports OK. `_scan_discriminated_locals`
  taints a local bound to a scalar-normalized env read and calls it a gate when the taint is
  discriminated by `==`/`!=`/`in`/`not in` against literal alternatives, or used as a `match`
  subject. Root-only (the read must be the whole right-hand side once a closed set of
  wrappers peels) and discrimination-not-truthiness, both measured against the tree — probing
  subtrees accuses a cache directory and a hash seed of being behaviour switches, and
  truthiness flagged 30 sites of which 27 were noise.

## 0.114.0 (2026-08-13) — **the weight-free mint is finally weight-free AND traceable: the mint child stops placing (offload hooks were fatal to `torch.export`), one unexportable class no longer costs the whole cell, the does-it-run proof moves onto the resident parent, and a modular component finally routes through its layout contract** — plus **two BREAKING removals: NOTHING quantizes at runtime any more** (the bnb-nf4 emergency rung and `convert`'s inline bitsandbytes lane are both deleted)

> **CUT FROM A PINNED COMMIT: `73f826e1`.** 84 commits since `v0.113.2`. The cut was pinned FOUR
> times (`2ce5dec0`/73 → `a194d916`/75 → `c8c2aea6`/79 → here) because a release cut DELETES every
> `changelog.d/` fragment while every lane PR MODIFIES one, so any lane ahead of the cut in the merge
> queue ejects it on a modify/delete, at roughly one CI cycle per recovery. Each re-pin folded the
> newly-landed fragment into the rows below rather than leaving it owed: PR #753/#754/#756
> (pgw#1202 — `ctx` generics, build-time generics, `task lint` parity), PR #755 (pgw#1206 D, the two
> BREAKING runtime-quant removals now named in this section's heading), and PR #757 (th#1867 S1).
> **th#1867's fragment is consumed here rather than left for the next cut**: its code is in this
> tree, so writing it under 0.115.0 would date-stamp it to a release it did not ship in — the same
> silent-release-note failure the `ls-tree` sweep exists to catch, in the opposite direction. The
> fragment sweep
> (`git ls-tree --name-only origin/master changelog.d/`, never `ls`) found **pgw#1180 cuts 2 and 3
> owed** — they landed after the last cut with no fragment, and one is written here by the cutter.
> That is the SECOND consecutive cut where the `ls-tree` sweep caught a silent release note
> (pgw#1181 was the first).
>
> **⚠️ THIS RE-KEYS — and the blast radius is measured, not assumed: THREE ROWS.** pgw#1176 makes
> the ENTRY the unit of identity (`ek1 = digest(class_hash × sm × toolchain)`) and moves the
> `envelope` axis out of identity entirely, so every key computed under the old scheme is stale.
> Queried on the standing hub: `cell_store` holds **3 rows, all `micro-diffusion`** — no real family
> has ever published a cell, so there is nothing in the fleet for this to invalidate. The re-key is
> free precisely because the thing it re-keys has never existed in production.
>
> **The toolchain axis itself is UNCHANGED**, measured in one environment with all 23 rows populated
> (triton and every `nvidia-*`/`bin:` row present, so not a comparison of empties):
> `toolchain e4b2b170438af354`, `declaration c757897a48482e33`, `loaded_libs 151aa8565a2f3cf0` —
> byte-identical to 0.113.2. So the re-key is pgw#1176's key-space change alone and nothing else.
>
> **THIS IS THE WHEEL THE CAMPAIGN IS BLOCKED ON.** pgw#1208's fix carries a falsifiable prediction:
> a mint child no longer places, so no offload hooks reach the traced graph, so **a 19 GiB model on
> a 48 GiB card should now export**. If z-image still refuses, that fix is wrong. The sweep opens
> with sdxl × A4000 for exactly that reason.
>
> **Cut WITHOUT th#1834 Phase 3**, deliberately — it had not landed and waiting for it would have
> held four families and an eleven-cell sweep behind a lane that is still rebasing.

- **pgw#1176: THE ATOM IS ONE GRAPH CLASS.** The compile loop compiled exactly one toy family in
  its entire life because it was built around a 36-entry all-or-nothing transaction — "the cell" —
  whose identity, adoption, durability, verification, arming and advertisement were all the same
  unit. Weight-free compile (pgw#1080) removed every reason for that unit to be big and the design
  never renegotiated. Three changes, landed together because splitting them creates a broken
  intermediate:

  **Identity.** `ek1 = digest(graph = class_hash × sm × toolchain)`, per entry. **The `envelope`
  axis LEAVES identity** and becomes a derived contract-manifest fact. `envelope_facts` digests the
  *union* of shapes/text_lens/guidance across the bundle — a property of the collection, not of any
  computation — so adding one aspect ratio re-keyed all 36 sdxl entries although 35 trace
  byte-identically (measured on `origin/master` @ `4dfdcd60`: two byte-identical classes moved
  `ck1-c4c134db…` → `ck1-48512ea3…` for one extra shape row). Per entry, the shape facts that
  genuinely affect tracing are already inputs to that class's graph hash — including the one real
  edge, a widened *dynamic* range, which re-keys through that class's own hash instead of punishing
  its siblings. `combined_graph_hash` demotes to `cell_key.manifest_digest`: a telemetry/coverage
  label the hub folds compile-health rows under, deliberately sm- and toolchain-free, and refused
  by `is_key` so nothing can resolve, download, verify or arm it.

  **Artifact.** Format 3: one `.pt2` + one `entry` block + its literals per graph class. The
  multi-entry `model.pt2` tarball, the `entries` map, and `combined_graph_hash` as identity are
  DELETED. `boot_key.fold` returns a key SET plus a manifest, so §4.27's <60 s target, the memo and
  boot-time adoption survive **strengthened** — a partial resolve now helps, where the cell key made
  30-of-36 a total miss and a full re-mint.

  **Arm.** The all-or-nothing arm is DELETED: `load_and_wrap`'s bind-all-then-wrap, the whole-cell
  key restatement, and `is_armed`'s every-target rule. `aot_serve.arm_entry` admits, binds and
  registers ONE class into a live `EntryDispatch` **registry** that entries join as they arm and
  leave when they de-arm; `disarm_entry` and the serve-path fail-soft de-arm cost one class, not the
  pipeline. The old invariant — *"a cell that cannot arm one of its graph classes arms none of
  them, because a partially served contract would be a silent subset of what the cell key
  advertises"* — is not weakened but made **vacuous**: a key advertises one class now, so nothing is
  left that CAN lie. This is what answers incremental compile-and-adopt.

  **And the constant clone is gone (pgw#1177, measured).** `target_constant_pool` handed back
  `value.detach().clone()` per FQN; `update_constant_buffer(user_managed=True)` makes no copy of its
  own, so that clone was the **only** copy in the system — one full duplicate of the target's
  weights held for the life of the arm, ≈5.1 GiB on sdxl's single `unet` target, in direct
  contradiction of §4.33 step 4. Its justification ("a post-arm resident mutation cannot silently
  change an armed cell") was backwards: eager sees the mutation, so it is the un-mutated compiled
  entry that diverges. What the clone also did — normalise contiguity — survives explicitly, per
  tensor, because an AOTI container takes a raw pointer.

  A deliberate, permanent SUBSET is now a legitimate steady state rather than a stage on the way to
  coverage. That is not only a latency story: pgw#1177 measured ~0.75 GiB of device memory per
  resident AOTI container, so a pod that arms its hot classes and leaves the cold ones eager holds a
  handful of containers instead of 36, on purpose. And "per entry" is the granularity of the
  ARTIFACT, never of the compile CHILD — pgw#1177 measured ~39 s of `env_seal.establish()` per fresh
  child, ~23 minutes across 36 entries, so a child that compiles several entries in sequence is
  strictly better and nothing here forbids it.

  `ck1 → ek1` is a §1.34 third-category re-key — a name persisted as an ADDRESS — and is executed as
  one coordinated cut with the hub schema, the resolve/publish wire, the
  `Arm.graph_contract_digest` proto change and the corpus purge. Priced now: the adoptable corpus is
  one toy family, so it costs one re-mint of a 3-class toy, and it can never be this cheap again.

- Typing: `mypy` now runs **strict by default** over `src/gen_worker`. A module
  added from here on is born strict; the 101 modules that were not clean at
  adoption carry a named, single-flag exemption in `pyproject.toml`. Measured at
  adoption: 413 `--strict` errors in 101 of 266 modules, so 165 modules were
  already strict-clean and are now locked there. `check_untyped_defs`,
  `disallow_incomplete_defs`, `strict_equality`, `extra_checks` and
  `disallow_subclassing_any` cost zero errors and are simply on — which means
  the `gen_worker.convert.*` untyped function bodies, previously unchecked
  entirely, are checked now.
- New CI guard `scripts/lint_mypy_ratchet.py` (`fast gates`): the per-module
  exemption lists may shrink but never grow, `strict = true` may not disappear,
  and a new kind of opt-out must be recorded before it can be used.
- Typing: the **test tree is type-checked**. Until now `mypy tests` did not
  produce a report — it refused to start ("Duplicate module named `conftest`"),
  so all 486 test modules had zero static coverage, which is where the doubles
  that lied about production contracts lived. `explicit_package_bases` plus
  `mypy_path = "src"` unblocks it; no `__init__.py` files were added, so
  pytest's import mode is unchanged. Measured once checkable: 2,016 errors in
  316 of 486 modules at the test posture, so **170 test modules were already
  clean and are checked from this commit on** — and a test file added tomorrow
  is born checked.
- Test code is exempt from the five annotation-completeness flags (a test may be
  `def test_x():`). Everything that catches a double contradicting production
  stays on: `arg-type`, `attr-defined`, `return-value`, `call-arg`, `override`.
- `scripts/lint_mypy_ratchet.py` now also refuses an undeclared wildcard
  exemption, and asserts CI actually hands mypy the paths the config covers —
  dropping `tests tests_v2` from the invocation would restore zero coverage
  with every check still green.
- Typing: the endpoint-**authoring** surface (`gen_worker.api.*`,
  `gen_worker.testing`) is free of bare generics and locked at
  `disallow_any_generics`. 30 sites: `Slot` → `Slot[Any]`, `RequestContext` →
  `RequestContext[Any]`, bare `dict`/`set`/`tuple` → parameterized. These are
  the types an endpoint author's editor resolves, so an unparameterized one
  silently erased their argument types at the seam they touch most. The
  burn-down list drops 69 → 62 modules.
- Typing/layering: `no_implicit_reexport` closed for `request_context`. Six
  call sites now import `_decode_unverified_jwt_claims` from
  `request_context._helpers`, the module that OWNS it, instead of through the
  package `__init__` — three other modules already did exactly this, so the fix
  converges on the form the newer call sites use. Burn-down 17 → 16.
  Two candidates were investigated and deliberately NOT taken: `chunk_upload`
  (the indirection is the seam a publish test monkeypatches — 13 failures,
  measured) and `cuda_root` (closing it strands a callable in the pgw#849
  baseline). Both reasons are recorded beside their exemptions.
- Fixed two unguarded `Optional` dereferences in
  `tests/test_device_peak_bank_pgw1205.py`. They reached `master` because CI
  runs only on `pull_request`: pgw#1205 and pgw#1202 PR 3 were each green
  against a base that lacked the other, and nothing re-checked the merge.
- Typing: `Slot[Any]`/`RequestContext[Any]` audited one signature at a time
  against a single rule — **a type variable that appears exactly once in a
  signature is identical to `Any`**, so it is worth writing only where `D`
  binds two or more positions. 11 sites converted, 14 kept with a stated
  reason. The one that matters: `resolve_slot` took `Slot[D]` *and*
  `Type[D]` and returned `ResolvedSlot[Any]`, throwing the type away at the
  point it was known; it now returns `ResolvedSlot[D]`, so an endpoint author
  reading `ctx.slots[...].defaults` gets their own defaults class instead of
  `Any`. Verified by A/B: with the TypeVar a wrong annotation is an error;
  with `Any` the same code reports `Success`.
- Typing: `request_context` (the `ctx` every handler is handed) is locked at
  `disallow_any_generics` and `warn_return_any`. `ctx.models`/`ctx.loras` are
  typed because the shape-preserving deep copy behind them says so once at its
  definition instead of leaking `Any` to every caller; `ctx.save_image/audio/
  video` return their real asset classes via a generic `_as_asset`; `ctx.slots`
  is `Mapping[str, ResolvedSlot[Any]]`, which is what its docstring always
  claimed; and `ConversionContext`/`DatasetContext`/`TrainingContext` name the
  defaults type they resolve instead of subclassing a bare generic. Burn-down
  62 → 60 and 26 → 25.
- Typing: the BUILD-TIME surface (`registry`, `discovery.discover`,
  `discovery.execution_lanes`, `entrypoint`) is locked at
  `disallow_any_generics`. 25 bare containers on the objects an endpoint's
  image build produces and reads — `CompileCell.shapes/targets/dynamic`,

- CI/local parity: `task lint` is the `fast gates` job rather than a softer
  namesake. It ran `mypy src/gen_worker` (omitting the 486 test modules CI
  checks) under `ignore_error: true`, so it could not go red twice over —
  pgw#718's failure was in `tests/`, a directory the task never looked at. mypy
  now runs the CI command verbatim and fails; ruff keeps `ignore_error`, which
